proposed_additions.question: If Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares uses a Power that explicitly Damages or Destroys Dahan, what happens to the Dahan and to the remaining instructions of that Power?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: Nothing happens to the Dahan from those explicit Damage/Destroy instructions. Ignore those instructions and resolve the rest of the Power normally. Bringer’s Invader nightmare Fear/Push outcomes do not apply to Dahan. This answer concerns explicit Damage/Destroy instructions; it does not prohibit the indirect Health-rule destruction already tested by Q86.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: Q85 asks whether Dahan or another Spirit named as the actor can deal real Damage through Bringer, not what happens when Dahan are the recipients. Q18/Q33 establish ordinary explicit Dahan harm, making this a consequential Spirit-specific exception. No existing prompt or keyed required outcome tests Dahan immunity under Bringer.
proposed_additions.ledger_gap: faq_rulings.bringer-real-effects includes this clause but maps it to Q85, whose prompt and answer omit it.

proposed_additions.question: Do general Range boosts affect only the Range box, or also numeric Range arrows inside a Power’s effect text? Does Shadows of the Dahan ignore those internal arrows, and does the old targeting wording on Sky Stretches to Shore make it subject to that limitation?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: General Range boosts apply to all Range arrows. Shadows of the Dahan changes only choosing the target of a land-targeting Power: ignore the numeric Range in its Range box while retaining the other origin/target restrictions and requiring Dahan in the target. It does not ignore Range arrows within effect text. Sky Stretches to Shore has been revised to function as a general Range boost and is not limited that way.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: Q19 distinguishes targeting Range from Gather/Push adjacency. Q28/Q72 preserve source/target restrictions. None asks whether a numeric arrow inside the effects is boosted, or the targeting-only scope of Shadows compared with general boosts; adjacency and numeric internal arrows are different rules.
proposed_additions.ledger_gap: faq_rulings.shadows-range explicitly says internal arrows are unaffected, but neither mapped Q28 nor Q72 probes that clause. The general-boost counterpart and Sky Stretches wording correction are also untested.

proposed_additions.topic: Internal Range threshold does not stack on Repeat
proposed_additions.question: Sap the Strength of Multitudes used its elemental threshold to increase its own Range. If that same threshold is still met when the Power is Repeated, does it add another +1 Range? What if the threshold Elements were lost before the Repeat?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: The existing Range change persists for the Repeat, but the internal threshold does not add another +1 Range. The Repeat keeps the prior boost even if the Elements needed for that threshold have since been lost. This is the specific published interpretation of internal Range boosts, rather than stacking the modifier each use.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: Q41 asks preservation of a Range/speed modification and loss of a non-Range threshold. It never asks the distinct branch where the internal Range threshold remains met and appears eligible to add its modifier again. The source explicitly identifies this as counter to a strict rules reading. Q72 concerns paying Shadows again, not an internal elemental modifier.
proposed_additions.ledger_gap: faq_rulings.repeat-boost includes Do not apply an internal Range boost twice but maps to questions/keys that never test it.

proposed_additions.topic: Repeat is a Power use, not another played card
proposed_additions.question: When a Power Card is Repeated, does it count as another Power Card played for Boon of Vigor or consume another ordinary Card Play? Does it count as using a new Power?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: A Repeat does not count as playing another Power Card, so it does not increase a count of cards played such as Boon of Vigor and does not spend another ordinary Card Play. It does count as using a new Power. Any payment required by the Repeat permission is separate from playing another card.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: Q40 tests delayed choice, Slow eligibility, card/innate limits and Element duplication; it does not test card-play identity. Not gaining the card’s printed Elements again does not itself test the no-extra-card-play outcome. Q82 supplies a separate-action Bringer example, but not the count-of-cards-played consequence.
proposed_additions.ledger_gap: faq_rulings.repeat-new-power maps to Q40, which does not ask or key the card-play/new-use distinction.

proposed_additions.topic: Unqualified Presence effects use island disks
proposed_additions.question: An effect says to Destroy 1 of your Presence and provides no exception for Presence tracks. May you destroy a disk on a Presence track to satisfy it and uncover that track benefit?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: No. Effects moving, destroying or otherwise doing things with Presence affect Presence on the island unless they explicitly say otherwise. Choose island Presence for that instruction; it does not remove a track disk or reveal a track benefit.

proposed_additions.topic: Innate availability without Energy or Card Plays
proposed_additions.question: A Spirit has used all its normal Card Plays and has no Energy left, but meets an unused Innate Power’s Elements. May it use that innate at its proper speed, and does it need a card in hand, another Card Play, or an Energy payment?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: Yes, unless explicitly specified otherwise by that innate. Innates are automatically available every turn and do not normally cost Energy or consume Card Plays; they are not cards that must be played from hand. Meet the Elements and other normal timing/target requirements. The usual once-per-turn restriction still applies.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: Q15 tests Element reuse, innate duplicate use, one target and Instead levels. Q40 tests what Repeat permissions may repeat; Q70 tests Lightning’s conversion allowance. None asks the ordinary no-Energy/no-Card-Play availability constraint after the card-play limit is reached.
proposed_additions.ledger_gap: Book Innates is mapped to Q15/Q27/Q29, whose actual prompts do not require this cost/availability rule.

proposed_additions.topic: No ordinary second paid card use or dual-phase use
proposed_additions.question: May a player pay a Power Card’s printed Energy cost a second time to use it again in the same turn without a Repeat effect? If a Slow Power is made Fast and used in Fast, may it also be used in Slow?
proposed_additions.predetermined_answer: No to both. A Power ordinarily has one use that turn; paying its printed cost again grants no extra use. Making a Slow Power Fast gives its normal use in Fast, not an additional use in each phase. An explicit Repeat or other stated exception is needed for another use.
